items.expected-result: memory_search over 25,917 real entries returns genuinely relevant results for queries whose wording does not lexically overlap the target content -- proof the vector leg, not just BM25, is doing real work; a plausible-looking but off-topic result list counts as a finding, not a pass.
items.command: Read 20+ real entries via sqlite3 against the snapshot to pick fair targets, then ai-raccoon --data-root <item1> serve --port 0 (pid 61648, :56226) + memory_search (tools/call over the MCP HTTP endpoint) for 5 queries across 4 different projects (jsaa, arasz-home-page, hermes-default, ai-badger), each phrased to avoid the target entry's own vocabulary.
items.evidence: Q1 (jsaa) 'why can't an orchestrator function use a countdown based on the real clock to cancel itself' -> top 5 all ADR-0044 durable-timer chunks, ranks 1.0-0.92 (query shares stem 'orchestrat-'/'cancel-' with content but not the key phrase 'wall-clock'). Q2 (arasz-home-page) 'proving a visitor's real world credentials on the backend rather than believing what they self-report during sign-in' -> top 5 span 3 different files (2026-08-11 plan, github-oauth-app-setup.md, ADR-0017) all genuinely about GitHub-OAuth identity verification, zero lexical overlap with query wording. Q3 (hermes-default) 'does the exact upper and lower case spelling of our product name need to match on every page of the site' -> top 5 all hit the actual app-name-casing/byte-exact-match hermes notes, zero overlap. Q5 (jsaa) 'was the bug actually caused by scanning the wrong part of the message...instead of the pattern-matching rule itself' -> top hits include ADR-0094 'admission reads the sender, recognition reads the subject, neither reads the body', directly on-topic. Q4 (ai-badger) 'what do we call a saved note that only shows a partial excerpt because it ran into a length limit' targeting entry id=18340 (the 'clipped' row in docs/retrieval.md) -> target hash 0eb20831... absent from top 20 of the default hybrid search entirely. Follow-up isolation: ftsWeight=0 (vector-only) also never finds it in top 20; vectorWeight=0 (FTS-only) with the near-literal phrase 'clipped candidate prefix not the query' ranks it #1 -- but the SAME phrase under default hybrid (fts+vector both weight 1) only reaches rank 18, i.e. RRF fusion buries a near-exact keyword hit under a poor vector score for that specific chunk.
items.observed-result: 4 of 5 queries: strong, genuine semantic retrieval across multiple real projects/files with no lexical crutch -- this is exactly the thing a 2-200 entry synthetic bank could not demonstrate. 1 of 5 (Q4): a real finding, not a pass -- a small markdown-table-row chunk that packs 3 unrelated definitions ('clipped'/'machine'/'harvestable') into one embedding evidently produces a low-quality vector for that chunk, and default hybrid RRF (ftsWeight=1, vectorWeight=1) lets that bad vector rank drag a near-literal keyword match down from #1 (FTS-only) to #18 (hybrid).
items.acceptance-reason: Retrieval quality checked live against the real bank as specified; the Q4 sub-investigation (fts-only/vector-only isolation) substitutes for a single black-box memory_search call because the surprising result demanded decomposing which leg of the hybrid fusion was responsible -- recorded as a finding below rather than smoothed into 'partial pass'. 4/5 strong hits plus 1 genuine, reproducible dilution finding is the real-bank signal this item exists to surface.

items.expected-result: PRAGMA schema_version does not move across repeated opens/writes/restarts on a bank whose schema digest already matches this binary's Ddl -- proving the ~40-statement CREATE-IF-NOT-EXISTS block is skipped, not merely fast, on a bank with real (not freshly-created) schema history.
items.command: sqlite3 PRAGMA schema_version before any open (baseline); ai-raccoon --data-root <item2> serve --port 0 (pid 66104, :56369); memory_stats + memory_search + memory_write over MCP; sqlite3 PRAGMA schema_version while server still running; kill 66104; restart fresh process (pid 66677, :56392, cold open, new PID/new ephemeral port); memory_search + memory_write again; sqlite3 PRAGMA schema_version + application_id + user_version after the cold restart.
items.evidence: Baseline (fresh copy of the real snapshot, before any open): schema_version=226895, application_id=-519479064, user_version=10. After open + memory_stats(13675 jsaa entries)/memory_search/memory_write: schema_version=226895 (unchanged). After kill -> cold restart (new PID 66677) -> memory_search/memory_write again: schema_version=226895 (still unchanged), application_id=-519479064, user_version=10 (both unchanged).
items.observed-result: schema_version never moved across an open, several real read+write operations, and a genuine process kill+cold-restart -- the digest gate correctly recognized the stored application_id already matched this binary's SchemaDigest and skipped the Ddl block entirely, on a bank with 25,917 real rows and real schema history rather than a bank created moments earlier by this same binary.
items.acceptance-reason: Directly observed via PRAGMA reads bracketing a real process restart, per ADR-0075's own stated discriminator. This is the scenario synthetic-bank runs could not distinguish from 'schema_version just happens not to move yet'.

items.expected-result: Opening a bank simulating a genuine pre-digest 1.20.1 install (model_migration table absent, application_id=0, user_version already 10) with 1.21.0 reruns the Ddl block, recreating model_migration, restamping application_id to the correct SchemaDigest, bumping schema_version exactly once, and leaving all 25,917 entries and their vectors intact.
items.command: On a fresh copy (<item3>): sqlite3 DROP TABLE model_migration; PRAGMA application_id = 0; record schema_version/application_id before opening. ai-raccoon --data-root <item3> serve --port 0 (pid 67874, :56460) to open+initialize, then kill 67874. sqlite3 PRAGMA schema_version/application_id/user_version + entries/vec_entries_rowids counts + PRAGMA integrity_check after.
items.evidence: Before simulated-upgrade open: schema_version=226896 (226895 baseline +1 from the DROP TABLE itself), application_id=0, user_version=10, model_migration absent, entries=25917, vec_entries_rowids=25917. After 1.21.0 open+close: schema_version=226897 (bumped by exactly 1 from the DDL rerun -- SQLite's internal counter only increments for statements that actually altered the schema; the ~29 no-op CREATE-IF-NOT-EXISTS statements for already-present objects did not bump it, only the one real change -- recreating model_migration -- did), application_id=-519479064 (restamped, byte-identical to the value on an untouched 1.21.0 bank), user_version=10 (unchanged, correctly not re-migrated since it was already current), model_migration recreated with the correct schema, entries=25917 (unchanged), vec_entries_rowids=25917 (unchanged), integrity_check=ok.
items.observed-result: Exactly the behaviour every real 1.20.1-or-earlier user will hit on their first 1.21.0 launch: full Ddl rerun triggered by the digest mismatch, model_migration table recreated, application_id restamped correctly, schema_version bumped precisely once (not once per statement, not left unmoved), and zero data loss across 25,917 entries and their vectors.
items.acceptance-reason: Every claim in the expected-result was checked against PRAGMA/table state read directly from the bank file, bracketing the exact simulated pre-digest state the task specified (DROP model_migration + application_id=0, user_version left at its real value of 10 since a real upgrading bank's schema is already current). No existing test exercised this exact 'real schema history minus the digest stamp' shape before this run.

items.expected-result: A genuine embedding-engine fingerprint change (not the model-set-twice trap that silently no-ops) triggers the outbox+relay migration (ADR-0076) at 25,917-entry scale: ToolGate refuses every MCP call for the duration, the relay drains every pending row to embedded with none left pending, and a mid-drain process kill is fully and correctly recovered by the next startup pass with no entries lost or duplicated.
items.command: Pre-flight extrapolation from the prior 200-entry run (~13s wall, 305ms relay pass): (305ms/200 rows) * 25917 rows =~ 39.5s of relay compute, well under the 15-minute cap, so proceeded at full scale rather than scaling down. Clean-run lane (<item4-migration>, pid 70674 :56618): confirmed baseline engine=local:bundled (model column NULL); ai-raccoon --data-root <item4-migration> --port 56618 model set local <path-to-the-SAME-bundled-onnx-file-verified-byte-identical-by-SHA256> (genuinely different fingerprint: local:bundled -> local:<path>, NOT the model-set-twice no-op trap); polled entries.embed_state and model_migration.finished_at every ~3-10s; tested a live memory_stats call mid-migration and again after. Crash-recovery lane (<item4-crash>, pid 78780 -> restart pid 82705): same trigger, killed -9 at 12,288/25,917 embedded (mid-batch), restarted, polled to completion; checked for duplicate (hash,path,project_id,context_label) rows and vector-row-count parity.
items.evidence: Clean run: CLI commit returned in 3.6s wall ('embedding engine set to local (...); re-embedding in the background'). Immediately after, memory_stats over MCP returned isError=true, text='model-migration-in-progress: ...try again once it finishes' with embed_state already 480 embedded/25437 pending -- confirms ToolGate refuses for the true duration, not just the commit. Polled to completion: embedded count climbed monotonically (928 -> 25917) over 357.1s wall-clock (T0=CLI-commit to embedded=25917/pending=0); a live memory_search after completion succeeded and returned correct hybrid results on the new engine. Final: entries=25917 all embed_state='embedded', 0 pending, vec_entries_rowids=25917, PRAGMA integrity_check=ok. FINDING: model_migration.finished_at-started_at read back as 6 seconds (1786912857 -> 1786912863), NOT the true 357s -- EntryEmbedder.DrainMigrationAsync stamps finished_at from the `now` DateTimeOffset captured once at RunAsync's entry (before the while-loop that does all the real batch work), not a fresh timestamp taken after the drain actually completes; invisible at 200-entry scale (sub-second drain) but a ~60x understatement of true migration duration at real scale. Crash-recovery run: killed -9 at 12,288 embedded/13,629 pending, lease_owner/lease_expires_at frozen at the last renewal (an in-progress, not-yet-expired lease -- expiry-gated-only reclamation per ADR-0076/SqliteModelMigrationLease, WHERE lease_owner IS NULL OR lease_expires_at < @now); fresh process (pid 82705) startup pass resumed draining (embedded count kept climbing monotonically from 13,024 with no regression) and finished 208.3s later. Final state: 25,917/25,917 embedded, 0 pending, model_migration.lease_owner/lease_expires_at both NULL (cleanly released), 0 duplicate (hash,path,project_id,context_label) groups, vec_entries_rowids=25917, integrity_check=ok.
items.observed-result: The migration mechanism is CORRECT at real scale on every dimension that matters for data integrity: refusal-for-duration (~357s, not just the commit), monotonic drain with no loss, and a genuine mid-drain SIGKILL fully and exactly recovered by the next startup pass -- 25,917/25,917 embedded, zero duplicates, zero orphaned vectors, both clean-run and crash-run. The one real defect found is an observability bug, not a data-integrity one: model_migration's own started_at/finished_at pair understates wall-clock migration duration by roughly the length of the drain itself, because finished_at is stamped from a timestamp captured before the drain loop runs rather than after it completes -- something only a real ~6-minute drain at this scale could expose; a 200-entry bank's sub-second drain makes the bug's effect too small to notice.
items.acceptance-reason: Both the clean-run and crash-recovery paths were driven against a real, live server at full 25,917-entry scale (not scaled down -- the pre-flight extrapolation correctly predicted well under the 15-minute cap and the actual run, ~357s/~208s, confirmed it), with the model-set-twice no-op trap explicitly avoided by using an explicit onnx path against a bundled-model bank. All data-integrity acceptance criteria (refuses-for-duration, drains-to-embedded, survives-a-kill, no-loss, no-duplication) are met. The finished_at timing defect is accepted as a finding rather than failing the item, since it does not affect correctness of the migrated data -- see findings below.

findings.finding: Hybrid RRF fusion can bury a near-exact keyword match under a poor vector score for a densely-packed chunk
findings.where: memory_search default hybrid ranking (ftsWeight=1, vectorWeight=1), ai-badger project, entry hash 0eb20831923593b5c2ac04c13769c9a8b0b2d13020765e30be022b7006a8ba78 (the 'clipped' row of docs/retrieval.md's terminology table, chunked together with two unrelated definitions 'machine' and 'harvestable').
findings.evidence: Query 'clipped candidate prefix not the query' (near-literal restatement of the entry's own text): FTS-only (vectorWeight=0) ranks it #1. Vector-only (ftsWeight=0) never surfaces it in the top 20 at all, for either this near-literal query or a looser paraphrase. Default hybrid (both weights 1, RRF k=60) ranks it #18 -- the poor vector rank drags a near-perfect keyword hit down 17 places.
findings.so-what: This is invisible on a small synthetic bank because there is not enough competing content for the dilution to show up in the top-N window. On the real 25,917-entry bank it means a query that would find the right answer via keywords alone can miss it in the default hybrid mode when the target chunk happens to be a dense, multi-topic markdown table row that embeds poorly. Worth a look: whether table-row chunking should keep semantically distinct definitions in separate chunks, or whether minRelativeScore / per-leg weighting needs a second look for this content shape.

findings.finding: model_migration.finished_at is stamped from a timestamp captured before the drain loop runs, not after it completes -- understates real migration duration by the length of the drain
findings.where: EntryEmbedder.DrainMigrationAsync (src/AiRaccoon.Infrastructure/Embedding/EntryEmbedder.cs) and ModelMigrationJob.RunAsync (src/AiRaccoon.Infrastructure/Maintenance/ModelMigrationJob.cs): `now` is `timeProvider.GetUtcNow()` captured once at RunAsync's entry, passed through to DrainMigrationAsync, and used verbatim as `finishedAt` in `MemorySql.FinishModelMigration` -- AFTER the `while(true)` batch-drain loop has already run to completion, but with a timestamp from BEFORE it started.
findings.evidence: Clean-run lane: started_at=1786912857, finished_at=1786912863 (delta=6s) in the model_migration row, while directly-observed wall-clock from CLI-commit to embedded=25917/pending=0 was 357.1s -- roughly a 60x understatement. Crash-recovery lane showed the same pattern on the recovering process's own successful pass.
findings.so-what: Anyone reading model_migration's started_at/finished_at to answer 'how long did the last migration take' (support diagnostics, an eventual progress/telemetry surface, a postmortem after a slow migration) will see a number close to zero regardless of how long the drain actually took. At 200-entry scale the drain itself is sub-second, so the bug's effect rounds away to nothing and no existing test would have caught it; only a real-scale drain (minutes, not milliseconds) makes the gap visible. Not a data-integrity bug -- embed_state/vectors/entry counts are all correct -- purely an observability defect in the one timestamp this feature exists to record.
